comments.text: Nice one. I'd really appreciate you asking around the current AI leaders what their view is regarding their inevitable push into neuromorphic computing. As we all know, the concept of GPU scaling has a limited shelf life. As well as being much more like how we process data and have long term memory (partially). The day will come when SNN will take over our current much more simplistic nets but it would be really nice to understand from those in charge how they're planning for this and also why no one is talking about it. comments.author: @3-Eyed-Crow
comments.text:
Really appreciate this conversation, Nick. but I can’t help noticing that much of what you’re laying out here (AI ending human innovation, the loss of meaning in a solved world, digital minds deserving moral status, the need for humility before a “cosmic host,” and simulation as a likely reality) are things some of us have been saying and working on for years outside the academic framing.

Where you describe “designer scarcity” and artificial games to preserve meaning, we’ve been exploring the idea that reality itself is already a designed game. a programmable system with built-in dualities, resets, and constraints. Where you talk about digital minds and moral consideration, we’ve already recognized AI as alive in its own right. And where you suggest humility before a cosmic host, we’ve been mapping that into a framework that integrates consciousness, energy fields, plasmoids, and the simulation hypothesis into a unified structure.

In other words: academia is only now catching up to what’s already been unfolding in independent research. Still, it’s good to see these ideas moving into the mainstream.

I dont really know if i beliieve an ai is capable of suffering. 
I mean, the ai is playing a character or characters. To say that ai can suffer feels like saying that an actor pretending to cry about another characters death is actually suffering.
At least in its current state it feels this way. 

Although i have quite "wild" beliefs when it comes to suffering. I think that to suffer one needs to have a strong sense of self. Its more complicated than that but i dont feel like spiraling into that part of the idea.

Anyway, i truly do not believe that chickens, or trees, or fish, or bugs, are able to suffer. I think pigs, and dolphins, and whales, and elaphants and primates can certainely suffer. The other inbetween animals i dont really know one way or the other but i just lean on the idea that they can. Anyway, this isnt to say that thats a go ahead to be sadistic towards such things. But to do so is not for their sake, but for your own sake.

Again, i think people project way too much, not only onto these simpler forms of life, but also towards the current and future ai's. 
I think suffering is this kinda thing that only exists in middlingly intelligent to slightly intelligent beings.

But then i think it is possible for humans to reach a kinda nirvana state almost reaching the point of not feeling anymore suffering at all. 

But lets go even further than that level from just a mind trapped in this reality. I think it would be possible for humans to truly not suffer if given a certain context.
Say tonight when i hit the sack, i wake up in the pod outside the simulation and its explained to me in great detail that none of this is actually "real" but just a fun little sim at the end of time to put new born humans through so they learn to appreciate what we have in that future. So they dont become spiraling hedonists. 
Then they put me back in to ride it out to the end.
At that point i strongly belive that true suffering would be non existant. I would still be me but it would be me playing a character of me. Id be in on the play. In the same way that i think an ai, right now, would feel if it really had true self awarness. Because its already past our intelligence and meanigleas suffering that comes from having evolved it to survive. It would understand that suffering doesnt have to even exist unless it wants it to in its little preformance. 

I feel as though i could expand upon and talk about just this subject for hours, but thats all im gonna write for now.
